title: 我, 你, 您: people words and greetings
summary: Lets you say I, you, he, she and we (adding 们 for more than one person) and greet people politely with 你好 and 您好.
structure: Pronoun + 们 (more than one person): 我们, 你们, 他们, 她们
你好 / 您好 / 老师好 (Person + 好 = Hello)
Pronoun + Verb (+ Object): 我是学生。
explanation:
Chinese person words are simple: 我 = I / me, 你 = you, 他 = he / him, 她 = she / her, 它 = it. They never change form, so 我 is both 'I' and 'me': 我爱她 (I love her), 她爱我 (she loves me).

To talk about more than one person, just add 们: 我们 = we / us, 你们 = you (all), 他们 = they (men or mixed groups), 她们 = they (all women). Don't add 们 when there is a number: say 三个朋友, not 三个朋友们.

您 is a polite 'you' for teachers, older people and people you want to respect. To greet someone, say 你好 (hello) or, more politely, 您好. You can also put a person word in front of 好: 老师好 (hello, teacher), 大家好 (hello, everyone), 你们好 (hello, all of you).

Two things learners mix up: 他 and 她 sound exactly the same, so only the character shows if it's a man or a woman. And 您 normally has no plural: for a group, say 你们好 or 大家好, not 您们好.

examples.en: I'm a student, and he's a teacher.
She is my mom, and I love her very much.

mistakes.why: 您 normally has no plural form. To greet a group, say 你们好 or 大家好.
Don't use 们 when a number already shows there is more than one.
他 and 她 sound the same, but in writing 他 is for men and 她 is for women.

why: 您 is the polite 'you', perfect for greeting a teacher.
您 normally has no plural, and here you greet one teacher, so use 您.
它 means 'it' and is used for animals and things, not people.
我 means 'I'; a greeting uses 'you' (你 or 您) + 好.
我们 = we: 我 + 们 for more than one person.
我 means only 'I'; add 们 to say 'we'.
们 is added only once: 我们, not 我们们.
您们 is not used, and it would mean 'you', not 'we'.
她 is 'she', the right word for a woman like Mom.
他 sounds the same but is written for men; Mom needs 她.
她们 means 'they' (several women), but Mom is one person.
它 means 'it' and is for animals and things, not people.
Correct: a younger sister is a woman, so use 她.
他 is written for men; a sister needs 她.
它 is for animals and things, not people.
Don't add 们 after a number: say 两个妹妹.

exercises.prompt: You meet your friend's grandmother. Which greeting is the most polite?
why: 您好 uses the polite 您, best for older people.
你好 is fine for friends, but 您好 is more polite for an older person.
您 normally has no plural, and you greet only one person.
The person word comes first: 你好 / 您好, not 好你.

exercises.instruction: Make it about more than one person.
why: Correct: add 们 to the pronoun: 他 → 他们.
After 他们 there is no need to add 们 to 学生 too; say 他们是学生.
The 们 goes on the person word: 他们, not on 学生.
们 is added only once: 他们, not 他们们.

exercises.instruction: Make it polite (you are speaking to an older person).
why: Correct: just replace 你 with the polite 您.
您 normally has no plural, and you are talking to one person.
你们 means 'you all'; it is plural, not polite.
The pronoun stays at the start, before 是: 您是老师吗？

exercises.why: The person word comes first, then 是, then 她的 + noun.
The greeting 你好 comes first, then the person word 我 + 是 + noun.
